s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of focal neurological deficits with evidence of cerebral infarction
salient_findings: Left middle cerebral artery distribution infarction on imaging
key_facts: 25-year-old woman
Presented to emergency department with acute neurological symptoms
Similar event 3 years prior requiring mechanical thrombectomy
History of well-controlled hypertension, obesity, migraines, and recurrent immune thrombocytopenia in childhood
Current medications: aspirin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin
History of tobacco use, which stopped after first event
Family history of similar condition in older sister
Vital signs: Temperature 37.6°C, respiratory rate 14, heart rate 78 beats/min, blood pressure 179/98 mm Hg
Initial National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score was 22
Laboratory tests showed elevated leukocytes, low hemoglobin, and low platelet count
Imaging studies showed left MCA M1 occlusion and left MCA-distribution infarction

shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of recurrent immune thrombocytopenia and current presentation of thrombocytopenia and cerebral infarction

raw.rationale: The patient's recurrent strokes at a young age, lack of traditional atherosclerotic risk factors, and family history of a similar condition are suggestive of Moyamoya disease. Additionally, the patient's laboratory tests and imaging studies do not show evidence of a cardioembolic source or antiphospholipid syndrome.

rejected.why: No evidence of a cardioembolic source

rejected.why: No evidence of inflammation or vasculitis on imaging studies

rejected.label: Atherosclerotic stroke
rejected.why: Patient's age and lack of traditional atherosclerotic risk factors make this diagnosis less likely
